claim: parseCopic keeps duplicate marker codes instead of rejecting or deduplicating them

triage.scenario: the filter `c.extractedColor && c.number` treats a JSON `"number": 0` as missing, so the row is dropped without a word, though `String(c.number)` would handle it. Codes are never deduplicated (unlike parseLego's names), so if upstream repeats an entry, two rows with the same code get written. A code is the swatch's identity, so the repeat would show up as a duplicate swatch or key.
triage.cause: truthiness test on a field that can be 0; no dedupe

claim: Brickset color names are written without decoding HTML entities
Outputs are written one after another with no atomicity, so a failed Copic write leaves the LEGO table already replaced and the outputs at different revisions

triage.scenario: `writeFileSync(PALETTE_FILES.lego, …)` succeeds, then the Copic write fails (permission, disk full) → legoColors.ts is new and copicColors.ts old; the comment "a failure leaves both files as they were" covers only render failures

claim: gen-brand-colors overwrites legoColors.ts with an empty palette when Brickset answers with anything but the expected page
Copic codes are sorted out of Copic's own order within the 0/00/000/0000 tiers
LEGO RGB parser checks the fields are digits but not their 0–255 range, so it emits an invalid hex color such as #3e72850

triage.scenario: `background-color:rgb(256,…)` makes `hex2` return `"100"`, giving a 7+-digit "#…" string. `oklab` reads the wrong slices and the row is written to legoColors.ts as an invalid colour. parseCopic validates `#rrggbb` and throws, but parseLego has no such check, so the two parsers answer "is this a valid hex" differently.

claim: theme-editor's base path is `/weasel/theme-editor/`, but fleet-dev advertises its URL at `/`
decodeEntities throws a bare RangeError on an out-of-range numeric character reference instead of its own named error

triage.scenario: a title holding `�`-style surrogates or a reference past U+10FFFF (e.g. `�` or `&#99999999;`) → `String.fromCodePoint` throws `RangeError: Invalid code point`, with no mention of the generator or the offending text, whereas every other unexpected reference throws `gen-brand-colors: no decoding for … in …`; HTML itself maps such references to U+FFFD rather than failing

claim: Copic rows with no name are emitted as `name: undefined`, which breaks the generated file's `readonly name: string` type
decodeEntities matches named entity references case-insensitively but looks them up case-sensitively, so mixed-case names fail to decode

triage.scenario: Brickset markup containing `&`, `"`, `<` or `>` (all valid HTML named references) → the `/i` regex captures `AMP`, `Object.hasOwn(NAMED, 'AMP')` is false, and the whole generator throws `no decoding for &`, though the table knows the entity

claim: gen-brand-colors writes to cwd-relative paths, so running it from anywhere but the repo root throws or writes outside the app
The upstream fetches have no timeout, so the generator can hang forever

triage.scenario: If brickset.com or raw.githubusercontent.com accepts the connection but never answers (tarpit, stalled proxy), `fetch` never settles and the script hangs with no message. `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` would make it fail with a clear error.
